EvidenceKind: native AWS S3 metadata request metrics with positive-only local population replay
Limitations: S3 request metric publication is best effort. Bounded missing points are not omission guarantees.
Latency magnitudes, request IDs, owner IDs, version/upload IDs, ETags, native XML lengths and timestamps are nonportable.
All measured operations use separately seeded keys and prefix filters; setup is outside the measured 120-second window.
The put-tags prefix includes its successful tagging write and one subsequent duplicate-key tagging request; its positive metric population is their combined population.

Broad native120s queries located the duplicate-tag request in a later metric interval. A separately observed native240s aggregate includes both tagging requests; replay does not synthesize aggregates or enforce native timestamp lag.

Three aborted preliminary lifetimes are retained in evidence with independent HeadBucket404 cleanup; only the final mature measured resource lifetime is replayed. The third preliminary lifetime positively observed BOE PutObjectAcl(bucket-owner-full-control) rejected with AccessControlListNotSupported.
Native bytes use wire-relative response lengths only where the native positive statistic exactly matches the consumed native response; other byte expectations project SampleCount only.
No replay expectation is created from an empty native metric result. Setup precedes the measured window; drain/reopen are deterministic local boundaries, not publication SLA assertions.
Native decoded SDK outputs and raw response bytes remain in evidence; replay outputs exclude nonportable identifiers and latency magnitudes.
